text: If the Earth suddenly stopped spinning for just sixty seconds, you would not gently float away. You would instantly become a supersonic projectile flying east at one thousand forty miles per hour.

Right now, even if you are sitting completely still on your couch, the ground beneath you is racing eastward like a hidden bullet train. Near the equator, the planet spins at over one thousand miles every single hour.

Your body, your house, your coffee mug, and the air in your lungs are all moving at that exact same speed. So if the solid rock of the Earth slammed the brakes to zero in one heartbeat, inertia would refuse to stop.

Anything not bolted straight into deep bedrock—cars, trees, streetlights, and you—would keep hurtling east at Mach one point three. Even your morning coffee would outrun a commercial jet before hitting the nearest wall.
Unless, of course, you happen to be standing at the North or South Pole, where you would just spin in a slow circle and wonder why everyone else is screaming.
